laws.title: RecordId is logical identity
laws.rule: RecordId MUST identify one logical Record across its accepted lineage and MUST remain distinct from revision, payload and locator identities.

laws.title: RecordId is opaque
laws.rule: RecordId MUST NOT derive from title, route, kind, language, timestamp, author, storage location, content digest, framework or mutable state.

laws.title: RecordId is globally non-reusable
laws.rule: Once admitted, a RecordId MUST remain reserved forever, including after archival, withdrawal or tombstone.

laws.title: RecordKind is constitutive
laws.rule: RecordKind MUST be fixed at birth and MUST remain identical across every accepted successor revision of that Record.

laws.title: Kind change creates a new Record
laws.rule: A change of ontological kind MUST create a different RecordId and an explicit relation rather than mutating the original RecordKind.

laws.title: Birth occurs once
laws.rule: A RecordId MUST have at most one admitted birth and that birth MUST be generation zero with no predecessor revision.

laws.title: Revision identity is content-addressed
laws.rule: RevisionId MUST be SHA-256 over the frozen canonical revision material and MUST change when any revision-bound field changes.

laws.title: Revision binds payload without interpreting it
laws.rule: The identity layer MUST bind the exact PayloadDigest supplied by the responsible kind schema and MUST NOT define semantic payload meaning.

laws.title: Succession requires exact predecessor
laws.rule: An accepted successor MUST increment generation by exactly one and MUST name the current accepted RevisionId as its predecessor.

laws.title: Identity and kind survive succession
laws.rule: A successor MUST preserve both RecordId and RecordKind exactly; changing either invalidates continuity.

laws.title: Lifecycle is mutable state
laws.rule: Lifecycle MAY change only through an admitted revision and MUST NOT change logical identity or constitutive kind.

laws.title: Tombstone is terminal history
laws.rule: A tombstone MUST be an accepted terminal revision, MUST preserve prior lineage and MUST permanently reserve the RecordId.

laws.title: Persistence is evidence not authority
laws.rule: Files, rows, serialized bytes, Git order, timestamps and build artifacts MUST NOT establish Record continuity without lineage validation.

laws.title: Conflicts fail closed
laws.rule: Incompatible valid candidate heads MUST produce an explicit conflict state and MUST NOT be resolved solely by recency, file order, timestamp or route precedence.

laws.title: Logical and pinned references are distinct
laws.rule: The system MUST distinguish RecordRef resolution of a logical current head from PinnedRecordRef resolution of one exact accepted RevisionId.

laws.title: Locator is not identity
laws.rule: A route, slug, filename or external handle MUST be treated as a locator that resolves a Record, never as the RecordId itself.

laws.title: Historical locator binding is not silently reassignable
laws.rule: A locator previously bound publicly to one RecordId MUST NOT later be silently rebound to another RecordId.

laws.title: Revision order is not epistemic order
laws.rule: A later generation MUST express temporal succession only and MUST NOT imply greater truth, support, maturity, visibility or importance.

laws.title: Representation does not mint identity
laws.rule: Changing renderer, framework, storage adapter, file location, serialization, route realization, build artifact or language representation MUST NOT mint a new RecordId by itself.

laws.title: Relations do not rewrite endpoints
laws.rule: A graph relation MAY connect Records but MUST NOT mutate, replace or retroactively redefine either endpoint identity or historical revision.
